newsitem.title: UK: Scottish scientists make new catalytic converter.
newsitem.headline: Scottish scientists make new catalytic converter.

text.p: Two Scottish scientists have developed a new breed of catalytic converter which could cut vehicle exhaust fumes more effectively and more cheaply than present types, Dundee University announced on Friday.
The all-palladium emission control device invented by Professor James Cairns and Dr James Thomson does not use expensive precious metals or rely on the complex coating technology of current models.
"Conventional catalytic converters use the precious metals platinum and rhodium," Cairns said. "Palladium has the advantage of being less expensive.

Cairns said their catalyst used a mixture of chemicals to complete the process of combustion started in the vehicle engine, mopping up pollutants such as carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and oxides of nitrogen which damage health and the atmosphere.

Conventional converters were expected to last for at least 100,000 miles (160,000 km) but the long-term durability of the new catalyst has yet to be established, though initial independent tests showed great promise.
Talks on commercial development were under way.
Thomson said the discovery came while they were working on a device to meet new legislation in California that will require drivers to show their catalytic converter is working properly.
